{{nihongo|'''Hinamori Shrine'''|比奈守神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Mino Province]].

'''Hinamori Shrine''' (ひなもりじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Gifu|Q45798|qid=Q45798}}, {{ill|Gifu Prefecture|Q131277|qid=Q131277}}.

It corresponds to Hinamori Shrine of {{ill|Atsumi district|Q11409326|qid=Q11409326}}, {{ill|Mino Province|Q864156|qid=Q864156}}, in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engishiki}}. However, there is also a theory that Hinamori Shrine of Atsumi District, Mino Province, is {{ill|Tejikarao Shrine|Q3517214|qid=Q3517214|lt=Tejikarao Shrine}} in the same city of Gifu.

It is near {{ill|Kamiakanabe Castle|Q17226097|qid=Q17226097}}.

=== Outline ===
The time of foundation is unknown. One theory says “Hina” means {{ill|Hida Province|Q1056535|qid=Q1056535|lt=Hida}} or {{ill|Emishi|Q932574|qid=Q932574|lt=barbarian peoples}}, and that this was a frontier defense point of the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yamato court}}. It is said to have been a base against attacks by Emishi from Hida, but geographically it lies close (about 1,200 m in a straight line) to the {{ill|Sakai River (Gifu)|Q4330698|qid=Q4330698|lt=Sakaigawa River}} (the {{ill|Kiso River|Q779607|qid=Q779607}} before the {{ill|Azuchi–Momoyama period|Q319531|qid=Q319531}}), which was the border with {{ill|Owari Province|Q514506|qid=Q514506|lt=Owari}}, so it is also inferred to have been a base against attacks from Owari.

It burned down in the {{ill|Battle of Funada|Q11614291|qid=Q11614291}} in {{ill|Meiō|Q1193841|qid=Q1193841}} 4 ({{ill|1495|Q6695|qid=Q6695}}). At that time, its founding date and origins became unknown{{r|g171}}. Since nearby residents had also disappeared due to war, it was not rebuilt immediately, and the current shrine buildings were constructed after the {{ill|Genroku|Q1325001|qid=Q1325001}} period. All buildings except the main sanctuary were rebuilt after {{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 50.

In the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}} it was called “Hidamori Shrine”{{r|g171}}. In {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 6 ({{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}}), the name was restored to “Hinamori Shrine.”

=== Access ===
*{{ill|Gifu Bus|Q5560101|qid=Q5560101|lt=Gifu Bus}} Akanabe-Mitahora Line: get off at “Kami-Akanabe” bus stop, 8 minutes on foot
**From platform 4 at {{ill|JR Gifu Station Bus Terminal|Q11226229|qid=Q11226229}} (north of {{ill|Gifu Station|Q1144885|qid=Q1144885}}), or from {{ill|Meitetsu Gifu boarding stop|Q11415771|qid=Q11415771}} (west of {{ill|Meitetsu Gifu Station|Q1109902|qid=Q1109902}}), take E70 “Shimo-Saba,” E71 “Takakuwa,” or E72 “{{ill|Prefectural Automobile Hall|Q11471893|qid=Q11471893|lt=Prefectural Automobile Hall}}”
